requested_by: the owner (decisions.md 6ecd8933: measure a static release build before deciding how the measured apps link), scoped by the coordinator 2026-11-23 20:55Z (option 1: musl static)
summary: gs-rest-service release: dynamic glibc (as built now) against fully static musl (flint package), runtime on the Spring workload and stripped O3/Oz against Go; non-gating
why: Go's comparator is fully static. Flint's glibc release build maps about 1.75 MB of shared-library text (gc.md 1.4). Fully static under ADR-023 means the musl target. Allocator confound, recorded as the coordinator asked: musl's mallocng replaces glibc malloc for the native libraries (openssl, llhttp, libpq) and for druntime's own pools. So this compares what a musl-static Flint app would really run on in production, not linking alone; an extra arm with mallocng in the dynamic build may separate it if that is cheap. Decision rule: the measured release profile switches to static only if Oz still passes against Go and no runtime metric gets worse beyond its interval; size and runtime then use the same static build, with the dynamic series as context. Method (tools/spring_binary_ab.py): both binaries pass 18/18 exact first; the manifest's phases unchanged; 6 runs per arm, the arms alternating (about 27 minutes); Go is not loaded in this window (its runtime numbers come from the gs-rest-multicore runs). Each metric is reported as the ratio of medians (static / dynamic) with a bootstrap 99% interval. The static Oz is `flint package --target linux-x86_64-musl --profile size` (0fef7c3c). m7 reports, locally, a 5,392,992-byte musl O3 static-pie that passes 18/18. Playbook M-5 records the mallocng confound. Runnable since m7-flint-cli's 365f29ca (validated end to end in a fresh worktree: O3 5,376,904 B and Oz 4,873,384 B, static-pie with no NEEDED entries, 18/18). The static arm's binaries are built ahead of the window by tools/musl_smoke.py (flint package --target linux-x86_64-musl, O3 and --profile size, both audited fully static) into .flint/musl-smoke/; the window builds only the glibc arm (release and size profiles) and loads both arms. Order: everything else, after phase1-builds-petclinic (owner order 74a746d1).
